newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Asia Product Swaps -Gas oil plunges amid glut.
newsitem.headline: Asia Product Swaps -Gas oil plunges amid glut.

text.p: Singapore gas oil swaps plunged late afternoon on Thursday due to a glut in the region as physical sellers were forced to store their prompt supplies in the absence of regional demand, traders said.
"Alot of people are trying to sell ... all the majors are offering agressively," one trader said.
February gas oil swaps was last quoted sharply down at $27.60/$27.65 a barrel, against midday's $28.20/$29.35.
The market traded in the morning at between $28.45 and $28.65 a barrel and in the afternoon at $27.70 and $27.60, brokers said.
March also nose dived and was last quoted at $27.55/$27.65 a barrel against midday's at $28.15/$28.30, one broker said.
The February/March time spread narrowed sharply to trade at 5 cents from Wednesday's 15/20 cents, reflecting the fundamental weakness of the market, traders said.
They said the market might flip into contango due to the absence of Chinese buying and high regional stocks.
"This could be the start of a new era as we see the Korean barrels hitting the market," one refining source said.
"The market could end up trading in contango for the better part of 1997 as was the case two to three years ago," another trader said.
South Korea's refining output peaked in January as crude units were running at full capacity, including the 450,000 barrels-per-day of new capacity which was brought on stream in the fourth quarter.
The build up of stocks, improved refining runs and low demand due to the Lunar New Year holidays have all combined to curtail Chinese imports, traders said.
Fuel oil is also poised to move into contango as oversupply continues to weigh on the market.
The February/March time spread is valued at near flat, one broker said.
February fuel oil swaps were last quoted slightly weaker at $110.50/$111.50 a tonne, down 25 cents from midday, brokers said. The market traded at $111.00 a tonne in the afternoon.
